correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 31–70 give an exact proof. With z=x² central, write the lower even coefficients as U+θV, the odd coefficients as B+θD, and separate the unrestricted top even coefficient. For F=B+θD and the corresponding F', the even bracket is z(Fσ(F')−F'σ(F))=z(σ(θ)−θ)(BD'−B'D); for the odd bracket the difference of the twisted even coefficients gives the other two minors independently in the basis 1,θ. Reduction modulo z^a and the injection by z use exactly the odd cutoff. The nonzero factor σ(θ)−θ remains invertible in characteristic two. Testing standard basis partners gives the center. An invertible S-linear change of coordinates takes a nonzero vector of valuation t to (z^t,0,0), leaving s^a·s^t·s^t partners; the central fiber has s^(a+2) lifts. Counting consecutive valuation layers, then summing the geometric series over all ordered partners, gives the stated sizes, multiplicities and asymptotic; even the largest noncentral order is strictly below the central one. The reported exhaustive small-ring histograms and F16 spot checks in VERIFICATION.md and verify_skew_commuting.py were inspected as finite corroboration, not executed or used to establish the universal claim.

value.rationale: The natural odd-cutoff central quotient gives exact pairwise commutation over a chain ring, not just an aggregate count, with a complete order distribution across arbitrary depth. In particular the characteristic-independent commutator computation establishes that same classification in characteristic two, where diagonalizing the involution into ± eigenspaces fails. This is substantive mathematical content even though the frozen presentation fails originality on its odd-characteristic portion.
